data.name: Arihant
data.gender_notes: Arihant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arihant is derived from the Sanskrit roots 'ari' meaning ruler and 'hant' meaning conqueror. In Hindu mythology, an Arihant is a spiritual conqueror or a Jain Tirthankara. The name is often given to children with aspirations of greatness and leadership. The name Arihant carries the meaning “Master, Ruler, Conqueror” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arihant usually hope their child will grow to embody master, ruler, conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner strength and determination to overcome all obstacles and attain enlightenment.
data.etymology: Arihant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Master, Ruler, Conqueror.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arihant total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arihant carries a deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it represents a triumphant and powerful figure. It stands for one who not only rules over their own lives but is also a conqueror of materialistic desires, worldly distractions, and inner demons. Naming a child Arihant is a way to instill a sense of courage, determination, and strength within them, inspiring them to lead and conquer their own life's challenges.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, an Arihant is regarded as a divine figure in Jainism. They are revered for their unwavering commitment to non-violence, truth, and self-realization. The name carries the profound meaning of a soul that has triumphed over the cycles of birth, death, and rebirth, attaining eternal peace and spiritual enlightenment. By bestowing this name upon a child, parents hope to inspire them to follow the path of spiritual growth and self-transcendence, ultimately leading to a state of inner peace and liberation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Arihant, meaning 'the conqueror of inner enemies,' represents a virtuous soul who has achieved self-mastery and inner peace, transcending worldly desires and material attachments.

historical_references.reference: Arihant, also known as Arihan, was a Jain Tirthankara, born in the 12th Arhant cycle around 870 BCE in the town of Sravasti. He was the 24th Tirthankara in the present cycle of Jain cosmology.

The term 'Arihant' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'ari' meaning enemy and 'hant' meaning vanquisher. Arihants are considered to be enlightened souls who have conquered their inner enemies, i.e., passions and desires, and thus attained moksha or liberation. They are revered in Hinduism and Jainism as ideal beings and role models.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Arihant' in Hinduism refers to an enlightened person who has achieved self-realization and lives a virtuous life. In modern times, the name has gained popularity in various contexts, including spiritualism, personal growth, and motivation. On YouTube, 'Arihant' is seen in the names of channels dedicated to spiritual teachings and meditation practices. On LinkedIn, it is used by professionals who wish to project a positive and enlightened image. On Medium, 'Arihant' is used by writers who focus on self-help and personal growth topics. The name is also used in various self-help and motivational books and courses.
